- [medium] Changing a setting in the ⋯ sheet closes and reopens the sheet: focus jumps to Done, then to <body> when the sheet closes (src/web-ui/routes/verse/Composer.tsx:879)
  Why: The ControlsSheet only renders while `compact` is true, and in a wide window `compact` is `fold >= FOOTER_FOLD_SHEET`. The fold hook (useFooterFold) starts again from 0 whenever its `labels` key changes (useFooterFold.ts:47). That key includes modelName, effortName, permissionMode and running, so any pick made inside the sheet changes it. Each time, the hook briefly goes back to fold 0: compact becomes false, and the ⋯ button and the sheet both unmount. The hook then steps back up to fold 4 and both remount. That remount runs useFocusTrap again: it records <body> as the element to restore, and focuses Done. I confirmed this with a scratch vitest run (jsdom, footer 10 characters wide, not a p
  Scenario: A keyboard user has the dock open, so the chat column is narrow and the footer folds to the ⋯ sheet. They open ⋯, Tab to the Model list and press Enter on 'Sonnet 5'. When the server answers, focus leaves the option they just picked and lands on 'Done', and the sheet visibly slides in again. They press Escape and focus drops to <body>, not the ⋯ button, so they have to Tab from the top of the document. A turn starting or ending while the sheet is open (`running` is in the key) does the same thin
  Suggested: Keep the sheet mounted while it is open, whatever the fold: render `{pickers && (compact || sheetOpen) ? <ControlsSheet …/> : null}`. Also stop the fold from resetting to 0 while an overlay is open: leave `labels` out of the re-measure while `sheetOpen || anyOverlayOpen`, or re-measure from the current fold and unfold only when there is room. If the footer really does widen past the sheet fold, close the sheet explicitly and move focus to the textarea.
- [medium] When the column widens or narrows across the sheet fold, sheetOpen/openMenus stay set: Esc no longer stops the turn and the sheet reopens by itself (src/web-ui/routes/verse/Composer.tsx:594)
  Why: Two overlay flags are never cleared when the fold changes whether the footer is compact. (1) If the column widens while the ⋯ sheet is open, fold drops below 4 and ControlsSheet unmounts, but `sheetOpen` stays true. (2) If the column narrows to fold 4 while a picker popover is open, the ControlMenu unmounts without calling onOpenChange(false); it has no unmount cleanup. Either way `openMenus[x]` or `sheetOpen` stays true, and anyOverlayOpen (line 594) stays true while nothing is visible. Before 3.10.1 this needed a phone-breakpoint crossing. Now any dock or sidebar toggle, or a window resize, can trigger it.
  Scenario: Reproduced in jsdom. Running turn, narrow column (sheet fold). Open ⋯, then widen (the ResizeObserver reports 1600px). The dialog is gone and focus falls to <body>. Focus the empty textbox and press Esc: onStop is called 0 times. Narrow the column again and the "Chat settings" sheet reappears without being asked for. Similarly: open the Model menu with ⇧⌘I, then toggle the dock with ⌘\. The menu unmounts, openMenus.model stays true, and Esc-to-stop stays dead until that menu is opened and closed
  Suggested: Compute overlay state from what is mounted: use `sheetOpen && compact` in anyOverlayOpen. In ControlMenu, call onOpenChange(false) in an unmount cleanup when it is open, using a ref for `open`. Close the sheet once the fold settles below FOOTER_FOLD_SHEET after a width change: have useFooterFold report a settled fold, or close it from the ResizeObserver width path. Do not close it from a passive effect on `compact`, which would fire during the transient fold-0 commit.
- [low] The fold never re-measures when the seat chip's capacity ring appears, so Send can overflow the box (src/web-ui/routes/verse/Composer.tsx:266)
  Why: useFooterFold re-measures only when the width or the `labels` key changes. SeatChip now draws the ring only when the reading is known (SeatChip.tsx:247, `ringTone(ring) === 'unknown' ? null : <CapacityRing/>`). The ring is 14px plus an 8px gap. Its presence depends on `seats[].capacity`, which the roster polls, and it is not part of the key. The row is `flex: none` and never shrinks, so extra width overflows instead of folding.
  Scenario: The composer mounts while the seat has no reading yet: no ring, and fold 1 fits with less than 22px to spare. The next seats poll brings a reading, the ring appears, and the right cluster grows by about 22px with no re-measure. Send is pushed past the composer box's right border (the box does not clip) until the width or a label changes. The reverse (the reading goes stale and the ring disappears) leaves the row folded further than it needs to be.
  Suggested: Add the ring's presence to the fold key, e.g. `ringShown = effectiveEngine !== 'local' && ringTone(ringWindow(currentSeat)) !== 'unknown'`, exporting ringTone or adding a small helper. Optionally also re-measure once `document.fonts.ready` resolves, since label widths change when the web font loads.
- [low] On every chat switch the footer paints unfolded first, because the first width comes only from the async ResizeObserver (src/web-ui/routes/verse/composer/useFooterFold.ts:41)
  Why: Workspace mounts `<Composer key={session.id}>`, so every chat switch remounts the hook with fold=0 and width=0. The layout effect returns early while width === 0. The width arrives only from the ResizeObserver callback, which runs after that frame's layout. Its setState is a DefaultLane update that React renders in a later task, after the browser has painted. The header comment says each step runs before paint, but that does not hold for the first measurement.
  Scenario: Narrow chat column (dock open), switch chats in the sidebar. For one frame the new composer's footer shows every label in words ("Accept edits", "Claude Max", "Effort: High"), with Send pushed outside the box. On the next frame it snaps to the folded icons. This is a visible flicker on every switch.
  Suggested: Measure synchronously on mount: in a useLayoutEffect with [] deps, `setWidth(Math.round(node.getBoundingClientRect().width))`. Or in the fold layout effect, when width === 0 fall back to `node.clientWidth` and proceed. Keep the ResizeObserver for later changes.
- [low] Footer fold resets to 0 and re-climbs on every 1 px width change (per frame during resize drags) (src/web-ui/routes/verse/composer/useFooterFold.ts:43)
  Why: The ResizeObserver stores Math.round(width) on every change, and the key includes the width. Any change while fold > 0 sets fold to 0, then the layout effect climbs back one step per synchronous commit, reading node.scrollWidth each time. ChatResizer calls setChatPanelWidth on every pointermove, so dragging the sidebar or dock edge while the footer is folded costs, per frame: 1 async render, 1 reset render and up to 4 climb renders of the whole Composer, plus up to 4 forced layouts. At fold 0 the wide permission, model and effort pickers and the ContextRing are mounted; at fold 4 they are unmounted again. A narrow chat column with the dock open is exactly when the footer is folded. Turn star
  Scenario: With the terminal or diff dock open, the chat column narrows enough for the footer to sit at fold 2–4. Dragging the ChatResizer (or resizing the window) re-renders the Composer 4–6 times per frame and mounts and unmounts its picker subtree every frame. The drag stutters even though the width moves only 1 px at a time and the right fold barely changes.
  Suggested: Keep the current fold when only the width changed. If the width shrank, continue climbing from the current fold. If it grew, cache node.scrollWidth for each fold measured under the current `labels` key and step down only while the cached width of fold−1 is at most the new clientWidth, with no reset to 0 and no extra renders. Reset to 0 only when `labels` changes. As an alternative or addition, coalesce setWidth with requestAnimationFrame and skip re-measuring while the ChatResizer drag flag is set, re-measuring once on drag end.
- [low] Icon-only permission-mode picker (fold ≥ 3) names the mode only in a native title, which never shows on keyboard focus (src/web-ui/routes/verse/Composer.tsx:731)
  Why: At fold 3 and above the Permission picker shows only its glyph (`iconOnly={fold >= 3}`). The mode's words are left in aria-label and in a native `title` (ControlMenu.tsx:188). ControlMenu uses a native title on purpose instead of the Tooltip primitive, and a native title appears on mouse hover only, never on keyboard focus. The effort control keeps 'High' visible when it folds, and the seat chip opens its own tooltip on :focus-visible. The permission mode, which is the safety-relevant one, is the only folded control with no visible words for a sighted keyboard user.
  Scenario: In a narrow chat column, a sighted keyboard user Tabs through the footer and lands on a small shield or pencil glyph. Nothing says whether the mode is Accept edits, Auto or Plan unless they open the menu. The composer's doc comment says 'the full words are each control's name and title', but the title is invisible to this user.
  Suggested: When iconOnly, open a tooltip on keyboard focus only. Wrap the button in the Tooltip primitive but open it only when the button matches ':focus-visible' (the SeatChip approach), which avoids the WebKit hover/blur problem ControlMenu describes. Alternatively, drop fold step 3 and go straight from fold 2 to the ⋯ sheet so the mode word never disappears.
- [low] A send in flight has no visible state: Send looks the same as when the box is empty (src/web-ui/routes/verse/Composer.tsx:846)
  Why: "Sending…" was removed and the in-flight state is now only `disabled` + `aria-busy`.   Scenario: The operator presses Enter on a long message and the turn POST takes a few seconds (the CLI is spawning, or the server is slow). The message is still in the box and Send has turned grey exactly as if nothing were typed, with no spinner or label. Sighted users get no sign the send is in progress, and it reads as "this can't be sent". Only screen readers hear aria-busy.

- [low] Composer310 fold tests leak fake scrollWidth/clientWidth getters: restore() is a no-op (src/web-ui/routes/verse/composer/Composer310.test.tsx:739)
  Why: beforeEach saves `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollWidth' | 'clientWidth')` and restore() re-defines them only `if (scroll)` / `if (client)`. jsdom defines both on Element.prototype, not HTMLElement.prototype. I checked: both descriptors are undefined. So restore() does nothing, and the fake getters (clientWidth = limitChars*8 = 80 px, scrollWidth = visible text × 8) stay on HTMLElement.prototype for every later test in the file.
  Scenario: The leak is latent today because the block is last in the file, but it will bite without warning. Any test appended after line 795, or run after this block under `--sequence.shuffle`, that reads element widths (overflow-based tooltips, or a ResizeObserver stub that reports a width) sees an 80 px footer and content widths derived from text length.
  Suggested: Stub the getters so the configured `restoreMocks: true` undoes them: `vi.spyOn(Element.prototype, 'scrollWidth', 'get').mockImplementation(function (this: HTMLElement) { … })` and `vi.spyOn(Element.prototype, 'clientWidth', 'get').mockImplementation(() => limitChars * CHAR)`. Or, in restore(), `delete (HTMLElement.prototype as any).scrollWidth; delete (HTMLElement.prototype as any).clientWidth;` when no own descriptor existed.

- [medium] BurnDown shows a made-up "Resets <now>" label and a false green verdict when resetAt is 0, NaN or before 2000 (src/web-ui/components/charts/BurnDown.tsx:155)
  Why: The new fallback handles a resetAt that fails isPlausibleTime by ending the axis at max(now, lastReading). The axis label still says `Resets ${f(xEnd)}` (lines 166-171), and the even-pace line still runs to that edge (line 231). Meanwhile projectBurnDown (line 135), burnVerdict and the aria summary (line 191) still use the raw resetAt. With resetAt = 0, every crossing check `at <= resetAt` fails, so exhaustAt and reserveAt are null and remainingAtReset equals the current remaining. The verdict therefore says the seat is fine however fast it is burning. With resetAt = NaN, remainingAtReset is NaN and the verdict prints "about NaN% left at reset".
  Scenario: A budget row carries a machine reset of "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z" (the epoch-0 leak this release guards against elsewhere). bindingReset's Date.parse returns 0, which is finite, so SeatBurnDowns renders BurnDown with resetAt = 0. Readings: 90% at now-6h, 60% at now-3h, 40% at now-1h, so about 10% per hour. Checked with the real chart-math: projectBurnDown gives exhaustAt=null, reserveAt=null, remainingAtReset=40. The card shows the axis label "Resets 3:42 PM" (that is now), a pace line hitting 0 at
  Suggested: In BurnDown, add `const resetKnown = isPlausibleTime(resetAt)`. When it is false: (a) label the right edge with the plain time and no "Resets " prefix, or drop the label; (b) skip the pace line and the projection path; (c) call projectBurnDown with a projection end of xEnd, or return the verdict {text:'Reset time unknown — not projecting.', severity:'unknown'}; (d) build the summary without formatTime(resetAt). Also make command-model bindingReset reject a machine instant that fails isPlausibleTime, so these seats take the TrailingWindow path.
- [low] axisTicks fallback jumps straight to integer ticks, flattening sub-cent or sub-percent series onto a 0–1 axis (src/web-ui/components/charts/chart-math.ts:116)
  Why: When the caller's formatter can't print the ticks faithfully, axisTicks retries at smaller counts and then with integer=true. For small fractional data, every non-integer candidate collides (for example formatUsd prints "$0.00" twice, or 0.005 as "$0.01"). The integer pass then forces step=1, so the domain grows 200x or more to [0, 1]. The data is squashed onto the baseline, even though a step of 0.01 would have printed faithfully.
  Scenario: SpendPanel or SeriesPanel "spend per day", or GrowthSection "Cost per merge" (both use formatUsd), where every day costs under $0.005, which is plausible for Grok or local-model autonomy. Verified: axisTicks(0, 0.004, {count:4, format: formatUsd}) returns ticks [0, 1] with labels "$0.00" and "$1.00". The spend line is drawn about 0.6 px above the axis and looks like a flat zero. The same happens with formatPercent (0 digits) for fractions under 0.005, which get a 0%–100% axis.
  Suggested: Before the integer pass, coarsen the step by powers of ten from the first candidate (for example try niceTicks with the step raised to 10^k × the magnitude until labelsFaithful passes, or add a `minStep` option to niceTicks). 0..0.004 with formatUsd would then give [0, 0.01] ("$0.00", "$0.01"). Use integer=true only as the last resort.
- [low] The label layout's width estimate ignores the Display size setting, so the no-overlap guarantee fails at Large and XLarge (src/web-ui/components/charts/chart-math.ts:200)
  Why: LABEL_CHAR_PX (and LineChart's AXIS_LABEL_CH, END_LABEL_GAP_Y and the gutter constants) are hard-coded to a 12 px font. But `.tick`/`.axisLabel` use --text-xs-size = calc(12px * var(--ui-text-scale)), and the appearance store sets --ui-text-scale to 1.125 (large) or 1.25 (xlarge). At xlarge the labels render at 15 px while layoutAxisLabels still budgets 7.2 px per character. It can accept a pair of labels that really overlap. chart-test-support uses the same constant, so the tests only check the estimate against itself.
  Scenario: Operator on Display size XLarge with a window wider than 1100px. Weekly BurnDown card whose plotW is about 290–335 px. Level 0 ("Sep 18, 11:46 PM" + "Resets Sep 25, 11:46 PM", 39 chars) is estimated at 281 px + 8 px gap, so the layout accepts it. At 15 px IBM Plex Sans the two labels take about 290+ px, so they touch or overprint. That is the defect this release was meant to fix. Dodged end labels likewise sit 14 units apart for glyphs now 15 px tall.
  Suggested: Derive the per-character width from the rendered font size instead of a constant. For example, read `parseFloat(getComputedStyle(wrapRef.current).fontSize)` (or the --ui-text-scale value) in the chart components and pass `charPx: 0.6 * fontPx` to layoutAxisLabels. Scale END_LABEL_GAP_Y and the end-label gutter constants the same way. Make axisLabelBoxes in the tests take the same scale.
- [low] formatTick switches format partway along one axis ("7,500" then "10.0K") (src/web-ui/components/charts/format.ts:92)
  Why: formatTick picks plain, K or M formatting from each tick's own value, not from the axis. A 2500-step axis crossing 10,000 prints the lower ticks as grouped integers and the top tick compacted with a decimal. That breaks the function's documented rule that every tick on one axis carries the same number of decimals.
  Scenario: Verified: axisTicks(0, 9000) with no caller formatter gives labels ["0", "2,500", "5,000", "7,500", "10.0K"]. This happens on AreaTrend, BarStack and LineChart cards without a formatY/formatValue whose counts peak between 7.5K and 10K. It is also reachable for M: 750K / 1.00M / 1.25M.
  Suggested: Choose the unit once per axis. In axisTicks, when no format is passed, compute `maxAbs = max(|ticks|)` and format every tick with that unit (for example `formatTick(t, step, unitFor(maxAbs))`, where unitFor returns 1, 1e3 or 1e6). The axis then reads "0 / 2.5K / 5.0K / 7.5K / 10.0K" or all plain integers.
- [low] Dark-theme heatmap: numbers on step-4 cells fall just short of WCAG AA contrast (4.49:1) (src/web-ui/components/charts/colors.ts:81)
  Why: quantityInk gives steps 1–4 var(--text-primary). In dark mode that is #f4f4f5 on --data-seq-4 = hsl(214 75% 48%), which renders as rgb(31,110,214). Computed contrast, using 8-bit rounding as the browser renders it, is 4.485:1. That is below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for 12 px medium-weight text. The code comment claims 4.5:1. The other available ink (surface) is worse at 3.8:1, so switching the step boundary does not fix it.
  Scenario: MindSection "Insights by kind and engine" in dark mode: any cell whose value is about 42–58% of the matrix max (quantityStep 4) prints its count at 4.49:1, a technical AA failure for small text.
  Suggested: Use a dedicated ink for cells near the surface in dark mode, for example `--chart-ink-on-quantity: #ffffff` in dark (4.93:1 on step 4) and --text-primary in light. Alternatively darken dark --data-seq-4 slightly, for example to lightness 46%, and update the comment's measured ratios.
- [low] The funnel's new neutral track is almost invisible: 1.18:1 in light, 1.14:1 in dark (src/web-ui/components/charts/plot.module.css:116)
  Why: `.trackEmpty { fill: var(--chart-heat-0) }`. --chart-heat-0 is --chart-grid, which is --border-subtle: #ececee on #ffffff (1.18:1) and #1f1f23 on #121214 (1.14:1). Funnel.tsx:118 draws every stage's track with it, so a zero stage is now blank space, not a visible empty track.
  Scenario: On Growth, a gate funnel has a stage at 0 (for example 'merged'). A low-vision operator, or anyone on a dim display, sees no bar and no track in that row, only the label and '0'. On a non-zero row, the unfilled part of the bar cannot be seen, so the bar length reads with nothing to compare it against.

- [low] Byte-cap compaction evicts the oldest rows for every seat, so larger setups lose the start of the weekly window (src/core/routing/capacity-history.ts:337)
  Why: Byte compaction is set by total file size (2 MiB, trimmed to 1.5 MiB). It drops the oldest rows first across all series, and that limit does not grow with the number of seats. A flat series writes 144 rows a day at about 111 bytes each, or 15.6 KB a day. With 8 days kept, 2 MiB therefore holds about 16 flat series (8 paid seats). Each value change adds rows on top of that, so busy seats fill it sooner. Once the cap is passed, compaction trims to 1.5 MiB by dropping rows from the oldest days for every seat. That removes the first days of the 7-day window that the weekly burn-down exists to show, which works against the release goal of keeping the whole window across reloads.
  Scenario: The operator has 5 Claude accounts, 2 Codex and 1 Grok, which is 15 series. Session windows change a few times an hour, so the file passes 2 MiB after about 5–6 days. Compaction trims it to 1.5 MiB, keeping only about 4–5 days. After a reload, each Command weekly burn-down starts mid-week with no rows before that point, even though `days=8` was requested.
  Suggested: Stop evicting whole days for everyone. Either scale the cap with the number of series (for example max(2 MiB, series × 8 days × ~25 KB)), or thin before dropping: during byte compaction, first downsample rows older than about 24 h to one per series per 30 min (keeping value changes larger than 1 point and reset drops), and drop the oldest rows only if the file is still over target.
- [low] A Codex weekly-only primary window moves to the 'session' series in its last ~5 h, splitting the weekly history (src/core/routing/capacity-history.ts:132)
  Why: `peakWindow` assigns each row to a series using `classifyWindow(engine, window, nowMs)`, evaluated at recording time. For Codex, a `*_primary` window counts as 'weekly' only while its reset is more than SESSION_WINDOW_MAX_MS (5 h 15 min) away, and as 'session' after that. For an account whose primary window is the weekly limit (the case the new test 'classifies a Codex primary resetting days out as weekly' covers), rows in the last 5 h 15 min before the reset go to `seat#session` instead of `seat#weekly`. The recorded series key is not stable for one provider window. The history stores the same physical window under two keys, and the web merge treats them as separate lines.
  Scenario: A Codex seat has a single weekly primary window at 92% that resets at 18:00. From about 12:45 its readings (92 → 99%) are recorded as `codex-x#session`. The weekly burn-down line stops at 92% about 5 h before the reset and never shows the final climb to exhaustion. A 5-hour series appears for that seat for those few hours only.
  Suggested: Give each series a stable key per provider window. For example, classify a Codex `*_primary` once per window lifetime: key it by its resetsAt, or record 'weekly' when the seat has no `*_secondary` window. Alternatively, record the window id beside the class and have `buildCapacityHistoryResponse` group by the class a window first had within the current reset period.
- [low] ASHLR_CAPACITY_HISTORY=0 only stops the background follow; both other recorders keep writing the history file (src/core/routing/capacity-history-api.ts:116)
  Why: The only place the env var is checked is capacityHistoryFollowRefusal, and its message says "disabled by ASHLR_CAPACITY_HISTORY=0". The other two recorders ignore it: the request-path recorder (withCapacityHistory → recordServerCapacityHistory, lines 176-179) and the daemon recorder (capacity-publisher.ts:282, recordCapacityHistoryFromSnapshot(snapshot, 'daemon')). They call appendCapacityHistory without checking the variable. The variable is undocumented, and its name and message promise an off switch that does not exist.
  Scenario: An operator sets ASHLR_CAPACITY_HISTORY=0 for the Verse server and the daemon so no new usage log is written under ~/.ashlr. The next GET /api/verse/budget (polled by Command, Fleet and the capacity strip), plus every daemon standing tick that sees a fresh snapshot, still appends rows to ~/.ashlr/routing/capacity-history.jsonl.
  Suggested: Put the check in the store so every recorder honours it: `if (process.env['ASHLR_CAPACITY_HISTORY'] === '0') return { appended: 0, compacted: false, error: null }` at the top of appendCapacityHistory, or a shared `capacityHistoryDisabled(env)` used by both withCapacityHistory and the daemon's defaultDeps.recordHistory. Keep the GET route serving whatever already exists. Document the variable in docs/VERSE.md and add a test that recording under the budget GET is a no-op when it is set.
- [low] History file opens lack O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO at the path hangs the Verse server and the daemon (src/core/routing/capacity-history.ts:245)
  Why: readChunk opens with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` (line 245) and appendPrivate with `O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW` (line 290). The regular-file check (fstat().isFile()) only runs after openSync returns. O_NOFOLLOW does not stop a FIFO, and a blocking open() on a FIFO waits forever for the other end. These are synchronous calls, reached from GET /api/verse/budget/history, from every successful GET /api/verse/budget, from the 60 s follow and from the daemon's standing tick. The sibling Verse history reader already guards this case (src/core/verse/fleet-history.ts:187-189, O_NONBLOCK 'if the path was swapped for a FIFO').
  Scenario: A same-user process leaves a FIFO at ~/.ashlr/routing/capacity-history.jsonl, for example a stray `mkfifo` from an agent's shell tool or a tool that replaces files with pipes. The next budget poll blocks openSync inside the request handler, and the whole Bun/Node sidecar event loop freezes: every API request hangs until the process is killed. The daemon's capacity publisher blocks its standing tick the same way.
  Suggested: Add O_NONBLOCK to both opens, guarded as elsewhere with `typeof fsConstants.O_NONBLOCK === 'number' ? fsConstants.O_NONBLOCK : 0`. Reads use `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`. Appends use `O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, which fails with ENXIO on a FIFO that has no reader. Keep the post-open isFile() check so a FIFO that does open is refused. Add a test that mkfifo's the path and asserts appendCapacityHistory and readCapacityHistory return promptly with an error or an empty result.
- [low] joinReasonParts rewrites '..' inside failure details, changing relative paths and git ranges (src/core/daemon/overnight-status.ts:268)
  Why: `cleanFragment` applies `.replace(/([^.])\.\.(?!\.)/g, '$1.')` to every failure fragment so that a doubled full stop ('failed..') collapses. The pattern is not limited to the end of a sentence, so it also matches '..' inside a token. Relative paths ('../dist') and git ranges ('abc123..def456') in a failure detail are silently rewritten. Those details carry `errText(error)` and git's own messages. This is the text the operator reads in the morning report to decide how to fix a halted landing.
  Scenario: A post-merge verify command fails to spawn with the detail `verify command could not be run: Cannot find module '../dist/cli.js'`. `recordOvernightIteration` stores `... Cannot find module './dist/cli.js' ...`, which points at the wrong path. Checked with tsx: `joinReasonParts(["... '../dist/cli.js'", 'git range abc123..def456 unreadable'])` returns `'./dist/cli.js'` and `abc123.def456`.
  Suggested: Collapse a doubled stop only at the end of a fragment or before whitespace/';', for example `.replace(/([^.])\.\.(?=\s|;|$)/g, '$1.')`. Apply the same change to the web tidyProse that this helper mirrors, and add a test with '../x' and 'a..b'.
- [low] The 'default recorder' test never touches the daemon's default wiring (test/daemon-capacity-publisher-310.test.ts:253)
